title: All seven primitive modes side by side -- and only the three that draw a surface may put a pixel anywhere

criterion.says: An example that shows rendering modes that are supported for mesh primitives in glTF.

acceptanceClass.because: The framing rule's own direction over seven static bodies, one per mode. TRIANGLE_STRIP and TRIANGLE_FAN have to triangulate to the SAME surface both sides agree on, which is the whole of what this decides -- and the odd triangle of a strip is (i+1, i, i+2) rather than a sliding window, so a naive walk faces every second triangle the other way and the disagreement is a silhouette rather than a shade.

blender.note: A release version, not a commit. Recorded so a red rung can be attributed to our renderer or to the oracle, and carried in the oracle's cache key so a version bump misses instead of serving a stale render. We do not aim to be bit-identical with Cycles.

subjects.name: MeshPrimitiveModes
subjects.notes: Attributes POSITION. Seven meshes at modes 0..6: POINTS, LINES, LINE_LOOP, LINE_STRIP, TRIANGLES, TRIANGLE_STRIP, TRIANGLE_FAN. Four of them draw no surface, and BOTH sides are expected to leave their pixels empty -- Cycles renders neither loose vertices nor loose edges, and src/gltf/Subject.cpp's DrawsASurface refuses them a part. That agreement is a finding and not an omission: a renderer that drew lines here would be outside the bound.

source.pinReason: the corpus-wide pin every manifest in this tree already cites

camera.derivation: The framing rule of src/gltf/Framing.h, quoted so the runner can refuse a mismatch rather than trust it. World bounds [-2.866, -4.0, 0.0] to [2.866, 4.0, 0.0], so centre = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0] and radius = 4.920767826264515 m. yfov = 2*atan(12/50) from a 50 mm lens on a 24 mm sensor height at sensor_fit VERTICAL. distance = radius / sin(yfov/2) / 0.6 = 35.142374570198, and the eye is centre + (cos20*cos35, sin20, cos20*sin35) * distance. clipStart is distance - radius and clipEnd is distance + radius.
camera.note: The glTF carries no camera, so the framing rule supplies one. Roll is 0 because the rule sets it: a roll chosen here and nowhere else would make this subject's placement a second determination competing with the rule.

light.note: The material emits, so nothing has to arrive for the picture to exist.

world.note: Declared and zero rather than left factory, so the picture is a function of this manifest and not of a Blender default.

material.note: Emission, one colour per glTF material, keyed by the name the FILE gives it. A material a primitive does not name is keyed by `<default>`, which is the format's own word for the material an undefined `material` selects.

default.note: The binary mask and the emitted colour in one render. One sample per pixel with the box filter at its RNA minimum makes Cycles evaluate the same predicate a centre-sampling rasteriser does, because the integer raster coordinate is the pixel centre and the sample never leaves +/-0.005 px of it. A still costs one frame, so the full 1280x720 is affordable here where an animated case has to buy its grid.

seed-shift.note: The same recipe with the sampler's seed moved. At one sample per pixel of a deterministic emission there is nothing for a seed to change, so any pixel that moves between these two renders is the oracle's own noise rather than a disagreement with us -- which is what makes this the instrument floor instead of an assumption about it.

notes: A coverage case. Its shading -- textures, metallic-roughness, any extension it declares -- is NOT what this decides; board:1363 records why no case takes the shading arm yet. Every primitive names no material, so one colour covers all seven and the comparison is purely WHERE the surface is.

subjectFrameFraction.note: The fraction of the frame the subject's projected area covers at frame 0. Recomputed by the runner on every run and refused on mismatch, so this line PINS the framing and never chooses it; seeded from that recomputation, it is a drift detector rather than a present-error check.
